title: Naturality of source independent expression shifts
statement: For every operation system, independent expression, input-family morphism and selected index, the existing sourceShiftComponent is natural: the source functor maps the shifted family morphism followed by the target component to the source component followed by the shifted source map, exactly as stated in the Lean declaration.

source.place: Step 2, source shift naturality in the independent input family.

proof.text: Rewrite both components by the source component decomposition: each is total limit applied to the pointwise reduction shift isomorphism, the input-shift endpoint transport and the generic expression shift, followed by the fixed total-limit shift. Naturality of the pointwise reduction shift isomorphism (a natural isomorphism of the reduction-shift lemma's construction) moves the shifted family morphism past it; the generic expression naturality square on the reduced morphism moves it past the expression shift. Apply total limit and naturality of its fixed shift; associativity and functoriality give the square.

mathlib_searches.query: Naturality of a composite source shift comparison through pointwise reduction and total limit
mathlib_searches.results: No exact project theorem; generic naturality APIs only.

mathlib_searches.query: Naturality of composite functor maps and shift commutation isomorphisms
mathlib_searches.results: Generic Functor.map_comp and CommShift naturality hits.

lean.statement:
theorem IndependentExpression.sourceShift_naturality
    {B : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} {X : I → Over B}
    (o : Operations l E) {W : Over B}
    (e : IndependentExpression B I X W) (K N : ∀ i, Integral l E (X i).left)
    (f : K ⟶ N) (i : I) (r : ℤ) :
    (e.source l E o).map ((inputShift _ i r).map f) ≫
        (e.sourceShiftComponent l E o N i r).hom =
      (e.sourceShiftComponent l E o K i r).hom ≫ ((e.source l E o).map f)⟦r⟧'
